A trailing edge cooling feature for a turbine airfoil includes a plurality of pins positioned within the interior of the airfoil near the trailing edge. These pins extend between the pressure side wall and the suction side wall of the airfoil, providing structural support while also promoting heat transfer. Each pin is elongated in the radial direction, allowing the pins to span a substantial portion of the cooling region and interact effectively with coolant flowing through the trailing edge area.

The pins are arranged in multiple radially extending rows that are spaced along the chordal axis of the airfoil. Within each row, adjacent pins define coolant passages between them. As coolant flows through these passages, the pins disturb and mix the flow, increasing turbulence and improving convective cooling of the surrounding airfoil walls.

A plurality of radially spaced partition walls is positioned downstream, or aft, of the pin rows. These partition walls also extend from the pressure side to the suction side and project toward the trailing edge of the airfoil. The partition walls divide the aft cooling region into discrete flow channels and help guide the coolant as it moves from the pin array toward the trailing edge.

Between adjacent partition walls are axially extending coolant exit slots. These exit slots receive coolant from the final, or aft-most, row of pins and direct the coolant out of the airfoil. The coolant is discharged through the trailing edge region into the hot gas path, thereby cooling the trailing edge while reducing thermal stresses and helping protect the airfoil from high-temperature combustion gases.

A turbine airfoil trailing-edge cooling design is configured to provide controlled and organized discharge of cooling air from the interior of the airfoil into the hot gas path. The design includes a series of radially elongated pin rows positioned within the trailing-edge region of the airfoil. These pins extend generally in the radial direction and are arranged in multiple rows to define internal coolant flow paths. As coolant travels through the trailing-edge cavity, the pin rows promote heat transfer by increasing internal surface area and disturbing the coolant flow, thereby improving convective cooling of the thin trailing-edge structure.

Downstream of the pin rows, aft partition walls are provided to form a set of defined coolant passages. These partition walls extend generally in the axial direction near the trailing edge and cooperate with the surrounding airfoil walls to create axially extending exit slots. The exit slots are located aft of the final row of pins and guide the coolant toward the pressure-side trailing-edge discharge region or directly into the hot gas path.

In operation, cooling air supplied to the interior of the turbine airfoil flows through the trailing-edge cooling circuit and passes across the multiple radially elongated pin rows. After the coolant exits the final pin row, the aft partition walls channel the flow into the individual axially extending slots. This arrangement helps maintain a more uniform and predictable coolant distribution across the trailing-edge span. By directing the coolant through defined discharge slots rather than allowing it to exit through an uncontrolled open region, the design improves cooling effectiveness and reduces the likelihood of localized overheating.

The use of radially elongated pins also contributes to structural and thermal performance. The pins provide support between opposing airfoil walls in the relatively thin trailing-edge area while enhancing turbulence and heat transfer within the coolant passages. The aft partition walls further organize the flow, limiting cross-flow and helping preserve the intended coolant path from the final pin row to the trailing-edge exits.

Overall, the cooling design improves management of coolant flow in the turbine airfoil trailing edge. By combining multiple radially elongated pin rows with aft partition walls and axially extending exit slots, the arrangement delivers coolant in a controlled manner from the internal cooling circuit into the hot gas path. This provides more effective trailing-edge cooling, better discharge control, and improved durability of the airfoil during high-temperature turbine operation.
